verdicts.reason: Quote states prescaler/step must be stable for correct increment.
Quote states software should de-activate timer before changing fields.
Describes a CPU limitation (a bus width fact); nothing to verify on the DUT, and the rule restates it as a prohibition the quote does not impose.
Descriptive observation of a hazard, not a testable requirement on the DUT.
Describes a software technique with no concrete verifiable behaviour; the third-read sequence is not specified in the quote.
The quote refers to a sequence that is not given in it; the rule is not verifiable from the quote itself and is software guidance.
Describes the rationale of an unspecified sequence; the sequence is not in the quote, so nothing concrete to check.
Quote says mtimecmp shall be written after mtime to clear pending interrupt.
Descriptive of a hazard/behaviour consequence with an uncertain actor; it is an explanation, not a requirement to check.
Quote offers a possible solution: software may set mtimecmp to all-ones; exercisable only in software flow, so check none is acceptable.
Software service routine behaviour described as a consequence of a suggested solution; the quote does not state a verifiable DUT requirement and it is part of a possible solution.
Descriptive observation of a limitation of the solution, not a requirement.

Quote states a working solution for any nonzero step; this is a suggested software technique and can be exercised in a scenario, but the actor is fine; strength MAY is acceptable. Check should be none as it is a software technique.
Quote directly states the interrupt is generated when mtime >= mtimecmp; checkable from signals.
Quote states clearing by writing 1 to INTR_STATE0.
Quote states a write to either mtimecmp half clears the interrupt source; this is DUT behaviour, so the actor should be slave and the strength MUST.

questions.question: Does a write to either COMPARE_LOWER0_0 or COMPARE_UPPER0_0 clear the interrupt only when the new mtimecmp exceeds mtime, or does it clear the interrupt source unconditionally (so it re-asserts if mtime >= mtimecmp still holds)?
Is the prescaler/step stability requirement enforced by hardware (e.g. ignoring writes while active) or only a software obligation? What does the DUT do if they change while active?
When mtime skips mtimecmp because of a step above 1 at wraparound, is the interrupt missed by design, or is it expected to be raised?
